author: marketing_c
protectedRevelations: Detailed research-object architecture, evaluation rules and portfolio recommendations

scenes.title: Faster in the wrong direction
scenes.viewerPurpose: Make the distinctive idea or tension understandable on first hearing. Introduce the book-specific proposal clearly and leave its fuller explanation for reading. Notice ideas growing faster than useful tests
scenes.composition: A small number of proposed explanations reach one test station.
addOrChange: Replace five simultaneous cards with two legible candidate sketches; make the station a real measurement surface, not a magical judging funnel.

cues.narration: A research AI needs more than better answers: it needs ways to discover that it is wrong.
cues.visualAction: A candidate produces more pages while its measurement remains unchanged.

cues.narration: The Frontier Is Correction proposes research systems built around tests, criticism, and mistakes that remain visible.
cues.visualAction: Bring the measurement and the candidate into the same view with the book title above.

cues.narration: AI can produce plenty of ideas, but useful tests and careful critics take time.
cues.visualAction: Hold the two candidates while one available instrument and one reviewer show the limited checking capacity.

scenes.title: Reality gets a reply
scenes.viewerPurpose: Follow an idea toward justified trust Value the critic asking an overlooked question
scenes.composition: A model’s prediction sits beside a measured result that does not fit it.
addOrChange: Add a reviewer’s brief question at the relevant measurement; no red cross branding an entire theory false.

cues.narration: The book follows the distance between an idea that sounds right and one we can trust.
cues.visualAction: Compare predicted and measured positions, leaving the disagreement visible.

cues.narration: An experiment may help, but so can someone asking the question everyone else missed.
cues.visualAction: A reviewer points to an overlooked condition beside the test, rather than replacing the result.

scenes.title: A record that can change
scenes.viewerPurpose: See a failure becoming useful to the next team Imagine lessons staying connected as ideas change Know the proposals must face their own tests
scenes.composition: An experiment record with a failed result and its reason retained together.
addOrChange: Add a second reader; use a single dependency connection from changed input to affected claim.

cues.narration: Even a failed experiment can help if the next team can find out what went wrong.
cues.visualAction: The second reader opens the failed result and finds its original reason beside it.

cues.narration: The book proposes ways to keep those lessons connected as ideas and assumptions change.
cues.visualAction: Change one input marker and highlight only the claim depending on that input.

cues.narration: Those proposals must also face tests that could show they are wrong.
cues.visualAction: Place the proposed record system itself on the test surface to show it also needs evidence.

scenes.title: The next decisive test
scenes.viewerPurpose: Leave room for disagreement inside AI-assisted science Ask which test could genuinely change a belief
scenes.composition: Two possible readings of a claim remain beside an unperformed next test.
addOrChange: Add two small distinct reviewer notes; leave the test result blank.

cues.narration: It is a view of AI-assisted science where people still have reasons to disagree.
cues.visualAction: Keep the reviewers’ differing notes visible at the same time.

cues.narration: Which next test would actually change what we believe?
cues.visualAction: Set the next test between the alternatives and finish before its result appears.
